summary: Blackton is five walled harbour towns: a Town Moot or a Lord's charter, salt and iron and sails, a road to Lerendor's protection or a free harbour, and an answer to Cocanoor, the Accord and the envoys from the south.

town_moot.name: The Town Moot
town_moot.desc: Five towns, five guilds and a lord with a harbour: the Moot is where they argue about the price of salt and the width of the quays. It decides slowly and is very hard to overrule.

lords_charter.name: The Lord's Charter
lords_charter.desc: Lord Haclton's charter gives the harbour-lord the last word and the guilds the first. It saves time at the Moot and costs the guilds a little pride.

free_towns_charter.name: The Free Towns' Charter
free_towns_charter.desc: Each town sends its own council to the Moot and counts its votes openly. No lord sits above them, and the harbour fees are the council's to set.

freehold_among_holds.name: A Freehold Among the Holds
freehold_among_holds.desc: Blackton is not a hold of orcs and has no wish to be one. Its walls are high, its guilds are rich, and its neighbours know better than to press a towns-people who can hire an army.

iron_market.name: The Iron Market
iron_market.desc: Orc iron comes down the Black Road to the market of Blackton and leaves again in Leren ships. Every bar is weighed twice and sold three times.

merchant_houses_spirit.name: The Merchant Houses
merchant_houses_spirit.desc: The great houses of Blackton hold warehouses on every quay and credit in every harbour. They lend to anyone, as long as the loan is secured.

leren_quarter.name: The Leren Quarter
leren_quarter.desc: A quarter of the harbour town is set aside for Leren factors, with its own warehouse, chapel and tavern. The streets there smell of tar and cedar.

free_harbour.name: The Free Harbour
free_harbour.desc: Any hull may moor in Blackton and any cargo may be sold, as long as the fee is paid and no questions are asked. The towns grow rich on being asked nothing.

between_two_shores_spirit.name: Between Two Shores
between_two_shores_spirit.desc: Blackton has settled its account with Cocanoor and with Notbuton, and owes neither a favour. The towns breathe easily for it.

quay_watch.name: Watchers on the Quay
quay_watch.desc: Harbour-watchers record every stranger who steps ashore and every cargo he carries. A spy who lands at Blackton is known by supper.

five_towns_militia.name: Militia of the Five Towns
five_towns_militia.desc: Each town keeps a company of townsmen at the ready, armed from its own armouries and drilled at its own expense. Together they make a host of surprising size.

privateers.name: Privateers of Blackton
privateers.desc: Letters of marque go out to every merchant captain with a swift hull. They hunt the war-hulls of the enemy and come home with prizes.

five_towns_stand.name: The Five Towns Stand
five_towns_stand.desc: The gates are barred, the walls are manned, and the harbour-chains are up. Every guild has pledged its stores to the defence.

shore_lanterns_spirit.name: Shore Lanterns
shore_lanterns_spirit.desc: Lanterns hang along the whole shore, and watchmen sit beside each. They show where the dead come ashore. They do not stop them.

the_town_moot.title: The Town Moot
the_town_moot.desc: The five councils meet in the great hall under the lord's banner. The lords wish to speak first, as they always have, and the guilds wish to speak first, as they always will.

blackton_asks_for_ships.title: Blackton Asks for Ships
blackton_asks_for_ships.desc: An envoy of the five towns stands before the Warden-King of Lerendor with a petition and a purse. Blackton asks for hulls and a promise, and does not say what it will pay if the answer is no.

corsair_sails.title: Black Sails Off the Five Towns
corsair_sails.desc: Black sails stand off the headlands, and the shipping guilds are in uproar. A message comes under a white flag: for a fee, the corsairs will leave Blackton hulls alone.

blackton_seeks_the_accord.title: Blackton Seeks the Accord
blackton_seeks_the_accord.desc: The envoys of the five towns arrive in Notbuton in their best furs, with a question the king has waited a long time to hear. Will the Accord take Blackton in?

strangers_in_the_harbour.title: Strangers in the Harbour
strangers_in_the_harbour.desc: Men from the south have taken rooms above the harbour tavern. They ask about ships, iron and the price of a berth, and they say they come from Nafeher and say little else.

an_answer_by_sea.title: An Answer by Sea
an_answer_by_sea.desc: A hull flying a friendly pennant comes in on the evening tide, with a letter for the harbour-reeve. The answer was yes, and the harbour-reeve reads it aloud on the quay.

focuses.name: The Five Towns
focuses.desc: Five walled towns share a coast, a language and a long argument. Lord Haclton calls the Town Moot to the great hall of the largest, and the guilds arrive with their ledgers under their arms.

focuses.name: Haclton of the Harbour
focuses.desc: Haclton holds the keys to the harbour of the greatest town and has done so for thirty winters. His seal is on every bill of lading from the Sea of Darkness to the straits.

focuses.name: The Town Moot Sits
focuses.desc: The five councils send their speakers to a single bench, and the bench becomes a court of its own. Whatever the Moot decides, the towns obey, or the towns leave.

focuses.name: The Lord's Charter
focuses.desc: A charter is drawn up and signed by the five councils, giving the lord of the harbour the right to speak last. The guilds read it twice, and sign.

focuses.name: The Free Towns' Charter
focuses.desc: The guilds draw up a different charter, in which the lord is a servant of the Moot and every town votes its own mind. Haclton reads it in silence and puts down his pen.

focuses.name: Walls of the Five Towns
focuses.desc: The walls of the five towns are lengthened and doubled, and the sea-gates are fitted with portcullises. A town may be besieged by land or by sea, and it will be ready.

focuses.name: A Freehold Among the Holds
focuses.desc: The Moot proclaims that Blackton is a freehold of free towns, owing nothing to Cocanoor and begging nothing from Notbuton. The proclamation is read at every gate and pinned to every harbour post.

focuses.name: Salt, Iron and Sails
focuses.desc: The trade of Blackton runs on three things: salt from the pans, iron from the holds and sails from the Leren yards. The Moot sends a clerk to each quay to keep a tally of them.

focuses.name: The Salt-Pans
focuses.desc: Shallow pans are cut along the shore and flooded at the spring tides. The brine dries in the sun to white salt, which is sold in every market of the Sea of Darkness.

focuses.name: The Iron Market
focuses.desc: A covered market of stone is built beside the great quay, where orc iron is weighed, graded and sold. Buyers from the Middle Lands and the North come every season.

focuses.name: Charts of the Dark Sea
focuses.desc: Tobin Greywater keeps the charts of the Dark Sea in a locked chest, copied from the notes of a hundred masters. His soundings are better than anyone's, and he sells them dear.

focuses.name: Harbour of the Five Towns
focuses.desc: A shared deep-water harbour is dredged between the towns, with quays long enough for the biggest hulls. Dockyards rise along its edges.

focuses.name: The Merchant Houses
focuses.desc: The great houses form a guild of their own, with a common strongroom and a common seal. A bill drawn on Blackton is honoured in every harbour of the north.

focuses.name: Sails to Sonargur
focuses.desc: Blackton hulls make the crossing to Sonargur each spring, laden with salt and iron, and return with timber and cedar. The captains are received in the Warden's own hall.

focuses.name: The Leren Quarter
focuses.desc: A quarter of the harbour town is given to the Leren factors, with its own warehouse and chapel. Where they go, goodwill follows.

focuses.name: Strait Guides
focuses.desc: Blackton keeps guides who know the narrow waters between the Dark Lands and the North better than the Lerens themselves. Their service is bought by the hull, and worth it.

focuses.name: Ask for Leren Ships
focuses.desc: The Moot sends a petition to the Warden-King of Lerendor, asking for hulls to guard the shore. It is carefully worded, so that Blackton can leave with honour if the answer is no.

focuses.name: Under the Leren Banner
focuses.desc: The Moot agrees to fly the Leren pennant beside its own, and to accept the Warden-King's protection in return. Haclton signs, and the Moot sighs.

focuses.name: The Free Harbour
focuses.desc: The Moot declares that the harbour is free and will remain so: no banner above its gates, no tribute from its quays. A free harbour is rich, if it can keep its friends close and its enemies busy.

focuses.name: Between Two Shores
focuses.desc: To the south is Cocanoor and its tallymen; to the north-west, Notbuton and its Accord. The Moot meets in closed session to decide which shore Blackton will lean toward.

focuses.name: Our Walls, Our Own
focuses.desc: The Moot rejects Cocanoor's gifts of black iron and builds its own walls instead, paid for by the guilds. A town that owns its walls owes no one thanks for them.

focuses.name: The Corsair Question
focuses.desc: The black sails of Cocanoor's corsairs have been seen off the headlands, and the shipping guilds demand an answer. Will the Moot pay the corsairs to pass, or arm its merchants to fight?

focuses.name: With the Accord
focuses.desc: The Moot agrees to sit in the Dark Sea Accord and defend the coast beside Dondor and Belonton. The vote is close, and the Accord is not told how close.

focuses.name: The Coin of Cocanoor
focuses.desc: Cocanoor's tallymen are admitted to the quays and Cocanoor's coin to the strongrooms. In return, the corsairs leave Blackton's hulls alone.

focuses.name: Neither Master nor Tribute
focuses.desc: Whichever path the Moot chose, the towns state it plainly: Blackton serves no master and pays no tribute. The words are carved over the harbour gate.

focuses.name: Strangers in the Harbour
focuses.desc: Men from Nafeher have begun to appear on the quays, asking after ships, iron and the price of a berth. The harbour-reeve reports it to the Moot, and the Moot considers.

focuses.name: Send Them Back in Chains
focuses.desc: The Moot has the strangers seized, shackled and put on a hull bound for the south. A note is pinned to the first of them: Blackton does not sell its harbour.

focuses.name: Southern Silver
focuses.desc: The strangers pay well, in a coin nobody on the quay has seen before. Haclton takes it, weighs it twice, and asks no questions.

focuses.name: Watchers on the Quay
focuses.desc: Whatever the Moot decided, the quay now has watchers: sharp-eyed clerks who note every stranger's face and every unusual cargo. A town that knows who has landed knows who to fear.

focuses.name: The Town Companies
focuses.desc: Each town raises a company from its householders, armed at its own cost and drilled on the common. They are no match for professional soldiers, but they have a very good reason to fight.

focuses.name: Crossbows on the Walls
focuses.desc: Crossbowmen are posted on every tower and gatehouse, with a stock of bolts and a spanner. A wall defended by crossbows will not be climbed easily.

focuses.name: The Harbour Chain
focuses.desc: A great iron chain is forged to bar the harbour mouth, and raised at need by a team of oxen. No hull passes it without the harbour-reeve's leave.

focuses.name: Sea Companies
focuses.desc: Boarders of the Moot's own, picked from the harbour wards, drill on the decks of armed merchantmen. They enjoy the work more than they should.

focuses.name: Militia of the Five Towns
focuses.desc: The five town militias are placed under a single captain, who is chosen by lot. The result is not as chaotic as the guilds feared.

focuses.name: The Towns Close Their Gates
focuses.desc: Every gate is barred and every chain raised. The five towns pull in their ships and their strangers and prepare to wait out the storm.

focuses.name: Privateers of Blackton
focuses.desc: Letters of marque go out to every swift merchantman. Blackton hulls prey on the enemy's trade and bring their prizes home.

focuses.name: The Five Towns Stand
focuses.desc: The gates hold, the walls stand and the guilds keep their stores open to the garrison. Whatever the world does, Blackton does not move.

focuses.name: Dead on Our Shore
focuses.desc: The dead have landed on the Blackton shore, and the harbour is full of pale lights. The watch rings the bells, and the guilds send every man they can arm.

focuses.name: Shore Lanterns
focuses.desc: Lanterns are hung along the whole shore, a hundred paces apart. They show where the dead come ashore. They do not stop them.
